features.title: The intelligence layer your
features.freeTierNote: Live monitoring and queue management are free, no time limit. Developer+ adds alerting, 30-day Queue History, Message Spy, and Incident Diagnosis — from $29/mo.

liveQueueMonitoring.title: Live queue monitoring
liveQueueMonitoring.description: Queue depths, message rates, and consumer counts — updated every second. Spot a stuck consumer or filling queue the moment it happens, not 60 seconds later.

smartAlertingSystem.title: Smart alerting system
smartAlertingSystem.description: Get paged before your users do. Set thresholds on queue depth, growth rate, or consumer count — alerts fire via email, Slack, or webhook the moment something's wrong, not after someone files a ticket.

queueManagement.title: Queue management
queueManagement.description: Drain, purge, or reroute queues without touching the CLI. Create exchanges, bind queues, and manage routing keys — all from the same dashboard where you spotted the problem.

performanceAnalytics.title: Performance analytics
performanceAnalytics.description: Historical charts for memory, disk, and message throughput. Spot a slow broker resource leak before it becomes a 3am page.

multiServerSupport.title: Multi-server support
multiServerSupport.description: Production, staging, and dev in one dashboard. No more three-tab incident response — all your RabbitMQ servers, one place.

messagePublishing.title: Message publishing
messagePublishing.description: Publish test messages directly to any queue or exchange without writing code. Reproduce bugs, validate routing, and debug message flow from the same dashboard.

dailyDigest.title: Daily Digest
dailyDigest.description: A morning health summary delivered to your inbox — queue depth trends, consumer anomalies, and the past 24 hours in one read. Know what built up overnight before you open a dashboard.

messageSpy.title: Message Spy
messageSpy.description: Browse headers and payloads directly inside any queue — read-only, non-destructive, production-safe. The management plugin can't show you message contents without consuming them. Message Spy does.

metricsPersistence.title: Queue History
metricsPersistence.description: 5-minute snapshots, 30 days retained. The management plugin forgets what happened the moment you close the tab — Queue History doesn't. See exactly when a queue started filling, even if nobody was watching.

incidentDiagnosis.title: Incident Diagnosis Engine
incidentDiagnosis.description: The management plugin shows state. Incident Diagnosis shows cause. Correlates queue backlog spikes, consumer drops, and publish rate changes into one readable timeline — 40 minutes of tab-switching, done automatically.

messageTracing.title: Message Tracing (Firehose)
messageTracing.description: Follow every message from publish to delivery — or failure. Full broker-level tracing in real time, with routing key, exchange, and payload size. Find out exactly where a message disappeared.

enterprise.title: Enterprise Self-Hosted Solution
enterprise.description: For organizations requiring on-premise deployment, complete data control, and enterprise-grade features. Deploy Qarote in your own infrastructure with full access to advanced capabilities.
enterprise.unlimitedServersDesc: Monitor as many RabbitMQ servers as you need
enterprise.advancedSecurityDesc: Complete control over your data and deployment

agent.title: RabbitMQ monitoring your agent calls directly
agent.subtitle: Below: the actual .mcp.json snippet, a real prompt, the grounded answer your agent returns. Eight tools shipping today, on every Qarote deployment — no Grafana plugin to wire, no Prometheus exporter to scrape, no copy-pasting between a dashboard and your prompt.
agent.snippetCaption: Drop into ~/.cursor/mcp.json or Claude Desktop config
agent.snippetHint: Mint the key in Settings → Agent Access. The snippet is shown once with your key already substituted.
agent.conversationCaption: What it looks like in practice
agent.youPrompt: Why is the payments.process queue backing up?
agent.agentResponse: Content-type drift on inbound publishes started at 14:03. Consumers reject malformed JSON (47% error rate over the last 10 min). Suggested fix: roll back the publisher that changed the payload format, or accept application/octet-stream in the deserializer.

whatCatches.title: Incidents as they happen. Anti-patterns before they bite.
whatCatches.subtitle: A deterministic rules engine watches live state for incidents, and a config scan flags the structural problems that turn into 3 a.m. pages. Every finding is something your agent can read back to you.
whatCatches.incidentDesc: Live, rules-based — fires the moment broker state crosses a threshold. Free and open source.
whatCatches.configDesc: Catches RabbitMQ anti-patterns in your topology before they cause an incident.
whatCatches.footnote: Plus topology visualization to see the whole graph, and alerting via email, Slack, and webhooks when something fires.

selfHosted.title: Run it entirely inside your network.
selfHosted.subtitle: Cloud-hosted when you want it managed. Self-hosted when you don’t. The self-hosted path is built so nothing has to phone home — including the AI.

offline.label: Offline license
offline.title: No phone-home
offline.desc: Self-hosted Qarote validates its license with offline JWT verification. No callback to our servers, no telemetry beacon, no dependency on our uptime for yours.

localAi.label: Local AI Explain
localAi.title: Root cause on a local model
localAi.desc: Point explain_incident at a local Ollama model and root-cause analysis runs on your hardware. Your broker state never leaves your network.

mitCore.label: MIT core
mitCore.title: Open-source detection
mitCore.desc: The incident-detection engine and the free MCP tools are MIT-licensed and open source. Read the rules, run the core, trust what it does.

agentSurface.title: Your agent calls the tools. You read the answer.
agentSurface.subtitle: Most RabbitMQ tooling stops at metrics. Qarote ships a deterministic incident engine and managed root-cause analysis behind one MCP surface your agent already speaks — so you debug by asking, in the chat you're already in.

connect.title: Connect broker
connect.desc: Point Qarote at your Management HTTP API over TLS. No exporter, no agent on the box.

mint.title: Mint a key
mint.desc: Generate an API key scoped to your workspace. Free incident tools, or unlock Explain.

wire.title: Wire your agent
wire.desc: Drop the server into your .mcp.json. Claude Code, Cursor, Copilot — all the same.

ask.title: Ask it
ask.desc: "What's wrong with my RabbitMQ?" The agent calls the tools and explains the root cause.

agentSurface.paidPara: Deterministic detection is free and stays free. explain_incident takes the incident plus the surrounding broker state and writes the root-cause line your agent reads back to you. Run it on our managed model, or a local Ollama model when self-hosted.

howItWorks.title: Connected in under two minutes.
howItWorks.subtitle: No Prometheus exporter to deploy. No Grafana to wire. No scrape config to babysit. Three steps from broker to a working agent surface.

step1.label: Step 1
step1.title: Connect over the Management API
step1.desc: Give Qarote your broker's Management HTTP API URL and read-only credentials, over TLS. It works against RabbitMQ 3.x and 4.x, single-node or clustered, including CloudAMQP and Amazon MQ.

step2.label: Step 2
step2.title: Qarote starts detecting
step2.desc: The rules engine begins scanning immediately — incidents, depth anomalies, dropped consumers, and config anti-patterns. No baseline period, no dashboards to build.

step3.label: Step 3
step3.title: Wire your agent over MCP
step3.desc: Add the Qarote MCP server to your editor's config and your agent can call every tool. Ask it a question; it does the clicking for you.

compareTeaser.title: Purpose-built where the alternatives aren't.
compareTeaser.subtitle: The built-in plugin is fine for a quick look. A metrics stack is powerful if you assemble it. Qarote is fast to value, multi-broker, and the only one that explains incidents and answers to your agent. It complements a metrics stack — it doesn't replace it.
